A DRM-Locked E-Book Cannot Be Compared to a Printed Book (video) | April

Some good points made.
A TL;DR :

  1. Usual justification for Digital Rights management (DRM) is that it is supposed to let ebooks behave like books by preventing unauthorized copying.
  2. DRM is a bad solution.
  3. Buyer of a physical book can lend, give it to others or simply re-sell it. Not a DRM ebook buyer.
  4. Unlike a real book, one needs to buy a particular DRM hardware & its software before buying the ebook itself. (This is like buying a chair & table before buying the physical book, IMHO, just that each book is tied to a particular chair & table).
  5. DRM tracks you and keeps extensive records of your reading habits, reading speed, what pages you read, etc.
  6. Unlike a read book, DRM can remotely erase your ebooks. Amazon has reportedly done that on Kindle devices.
  7. The goal of DRM is thus to hoard all benefits of digital technology with the publisher, rather than the end user.
